Answer: C
Reason: The follow-up chest X-ray (Figure 2) demonstrates new, dense opacification of the right lung compared to the initial clear film (Figure 1), which is characteristic of a bacterial superinfection complicating the recovery phase of viral pneumonia. This radiographic progression aligns with sudden clinical worsening 18 days after admission, whereas options like pneumothorax or isolated effusion do not match the parenchymal consolidation seen.
